- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak in early horizon (1–7 days); model underreacts to recent price drops; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for 1–3 day horizon.
- For 10+ day horizons, model tends to lag behind true price movements; add 0.5–2% upward bias to catch momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model misreads trend direction; adjust forecast to average of recent 3–5 day sentiment-weighted mean.
